evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.248: in commūnī vītā et vulgārī hominum cōnsuētūdine (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of the many, so also commonplace; the adverb is vulgō, commonly (see popular).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 5.16.2: cōnsōlātiō pervulgāta quidem illa maximē

phrases.latin: vulgāre amīcī nōmen, sed rāra est fidēs
phrases.english: the name of friend is common, but loyalty is rare

phrases.latin: quibus nōn vulgāris in cursū gradus, sed mollis alternō crūrum explicātū glomerātiō
phrases.english: whose pace in running is not the common one, but a soft rolling gait, the legs thrown out by turns

sources: Lewis & Short: vulgaris · Lewis & Short: pervulgo
